lesson.title: Two clocks
lesson.body: The 12-hour clock goes round twice a day: a.m. before noon, p.m. after it. The 24-hour clock counts the hours from midnight, from 00:00 to 23:59, so it needs no a.m. or p.m.

lesson.title: Changing back
lesson.body: After noon, add 12 to the hours: 3:45 p.m. is 15:45. To go back, take 12 away: 19:20 is 7:20 p.m. Just after midnight the hours are 00, so 12:30 a.m. is 00:30.

lesson.title: Count on
lesson.body: Times are not ordinary numbers: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on instead. From 8:45 to 9:00 is 15 minutes, then 9:00 to 13:00 is 4 hours, then 13:00 to 13:20 is 20 minutes.

lesson.title: Across noon or midnight
lesson.body: Split the time at noon or at midnight. From 9:00 p.m. to midnight is 3 hours, and from midnight to 5:30 a.m. is 5 hours 30 minutes: 8 hours 30 minutes in all.

lesson.title: Adding a length of time
lesson.body: Add the hours, then the minutes. When the minutes reach 60 or more, carry 60 of them as 1 hour: 14:50 and 1 hour 45 minutes is 15:95, which is 16:35.

lesson.title: Working backwards
lesson.body: To find a start time, take the length of time away from the end time. Borrow an hour as 60 minutes when you need more minutes: 11:10 is 10 hours 70 minutes, and taking away 1 hour 25 minutes leaves 9:45.

lesson.title: Ahead and behind
lesson.body: Countries east of the Philippines are ahead of Manila: Tokyo is 1 hour ahead. Countries to the west are behind: Dubai is 4 hours behind. Ahead, add the hours; behind, take them away.

lesson.title: Flying across time zones
lesson.body: For a flight, first add the flying time in Manila time. Then change the landing time to the time where the plane lands.

templates.construct: Say how many hours after midnight a 12-hour time is

formats.prompt: The 24-hour clock counts the hours from midnight. How many whole hours after midnight is {clock12(t)}?

hints: Before noon, the hours are the ones the 12-hour clock shows.
After noon, add the 12 hours from midnight to noon.
{h > 12 ? 'It is after noon, so add 12.' : 'It is before noon, so the hours stay as they are.'}
steps: {h < 12 ? 'Before noon the hours stay as they are' : 'After noon, add 12'}
{h > 12 ? h - 12 : h}{h > 12 ? ' + 12 = ' : ' hours after midnight'}{h > 12 ? fmt(answer) : ''}
templates.explain: {clock12(t)} is {answer} whole hours after midnight, so on the 24-hour clock it is {clock(t)}.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the hour the 12-hour clock shows. After noon, add the 12 hours from midnight to noon: {value} + 12 = {answer}.
{value} hours after midnight is in the evening. {clock12(t)} is before noon, so it is {answer} hours after midnight.

hints: Is it before noon or after noon?

{h == 0 ? 'Just after midnight, the hours are 00.' : (h < 12 ? 'Before noon, the hours stay as they are.' : (h == 12 ? 'From noon to 1 p.m., the hours stay 12.' : 'After noon, add 12 to the hours.'))}
The minutes stay as they are: {m < 10 ? '0' : ''}{m}.

distractors.feedback: {clock(value)} means {clock12(value)} in 12-hour time. After noon, add 12 to the hours: {clock(answer)}.
{clock(value)} means {clock12(value)} in 12-hour time. {h == 0 ? 'Just after midnight the hours are 00' : 'Before noon the hours stay as they are'}: {clock(answer)}.

hints: {h} is more than 12, so the time is after noon: p.m.
Take 12 away from the hours.
It is not {clock12(t - 60)}: that would be {clock(t - 60)}.
templates.explain: {h} − 12 = {h - 12}, so {clock12(t)} is the same time as {clock(t)}.

distractors.feedback: {clock12(value)} would be {clock(value)}. {clock(t)} is after noon, so its 12-hour time ends in p.m.
{clock12(value)} would be {clock(value)}. Take 12 from the hours, not 10: {h} − 12 = {h - 12}.
{clock12(value)} would be {clock(value)}. Take 12 from the hours: {h} − 12 = {h - 12}.

templates.construct: Find a length of time by counting on

formats.prompt: A bus leaves the terminal at {clock(s)} and arrives at {clock(e)}. How many minutes does the trip take?
A school fair opens at {clock(s)} and the last game ends at {clock(e)}. How many minutes is that?

hints: Count on from {clock(s)} to the next full hour.
{clock(s)} to {clock(next)} is {60 - sm} minutes.
Then on to {clock(e)} is {e - next} more minutes.
templates.explain: Count on: {60 - sm} minutes to {clock(next)}, then {e - next} more. That is {answer} minutes.

distractors.feedback: {value} takes {sh * 100 + sm} from {floor(e / 60) * 100 + e % 60} as if they were ordinary numbers. An hour has 60 minutes, not 100: count on from {clock(s)} instead.
{value} counts whole hours, {clock(sh * 60)} to {clock(floor(e / 60) * 60)}. Count the minutes too: from {clock(s)} to {clock(e)}.

templates.construct: Find a length of time across noon

formats.prompt: A store is open from {clock12(s)} to {clock12(e)} every day. How long is it open?
A clinic is open from {clock12(s)} to {clock12(e)} on Saturdays. How long is it open?

hints: Split the time at noon.
{clock12(s)} to 12:00 noon is {hm(720 - s)}.
It is not {hm(d - 720)}: that takes {clock12(s)} from {clock12(e)} as if both were in the morning.
templates.explain: {hm(720 - s)} before noon and {hm(e - 720)} after it: {hm(answer)}.

distractors.feedback: {hm(value)} takes {clock12(s)} from {clock12(e)} as if both were in the morning. Split at noon: {hm(720 - s)} before it and {hm(e - 720)} after.
{hm(value)} is an hour short. Split at noon: {hm(720 - s)} before it and {hm(e - 720)} after.
{hm(value)} is an hour too long. Split at noon: {hm(720 - s)} before it and {hm(e - 720)} after.

templates.construct: Find a length of time across midnight

formats.prompt: An overnight bus leaves at {clock(s)} and arrives at {clock(e)} the next day. How long is the trip?

hints: Split the trip at midnight.
{clock(s)} to midnight is {hm(1440 - s)}.
Midnight to {clock(e)} is {hm(e)}.
templates.explain: {hm(1440 - s)} before midnight and {hm(e)} after it: {hm(answer)}.

distractors.feedback: {hm(value)} is the time from {clock(e)} to {clock(s)} on the same day. The bus arrives the next day: split the trip at midnight.
{hm(value)} only reaches midnight. Add the {hm(e)} after it.
{hm(value)} is an hour short: {hm(1440 - s)} before midnight and {hm(e)} after.

templates.construct: Add a length of time to a 24-hour time

formats.prompt: A movie starts at {clock(s)} and runs for {hm(d)}. At what time does it end?
A bus leaves at {clock(s)}, and the trip takes {hm(d)}. At what time does it arrive?

hints: Add the hours, then the minutes.
{clock(s)} + {dh} hour{dh == 1 ? '' : 's'} = {clock(s + dh * 60)}.
Then {s % 60} + {d % 60} = {s % 60 + d % 60} minutes, which is {hm(s % 60 + d % 60)}.
steps: {s % 60} + {d % 60} = {s % 60 + d % 60} minutes: carry 60 of them as 1 hour

distractors.feedback: {clock(value)} is an hour early. {s % 60} + {d % 60} = {s % 60 + d % 60} minutes, which is {hm(s % 60 + d % 60)}: carry the hour.
{clock(value)} adds the {d % 60} minutes but not the {dh} hour{dh == 1 ? '' : 's'}.

templates.construct: Take a length of time from a 24-hour time

formats.prompt: A field trip ends at {clock(e)}. It lasted {hm(d)}. At what time did it start?
A bus arrives at {clock(e)} after a trip of {hm(d)}. At what time did it leave?

hints: Take the length of time away from the end time.
Take away the hours first: {clock(e)} − {dh} hour{dh == 1 ? '' : 's'} = {clock(mid)}.
{e % 60} minutes is less than {d % 60}, so borrow an hour as 60 minutes.

distractors.feedback: {clock(value)} adds the {hm(d)}. The start is before the end: take the time away.
{clock(value)} is an hour late. When you borrow 60 minutes, take 1 from the hours too.

templates.construct: Work back from a deadline through two lengths of time

formats.prompt: Ben must be at school by {clock(e)}. Getting ready takes {hm(r)}, and the walk to school takes {w} minutes. What is the latest time Ben can wake up?

hints: Work backwards from {clock(e)}.
Together, getting ready and walking take {hm(r + w)}.
{clock(e)} − {hm(r + w)} = ?
steps: Getting ready and walking: {hm(r)} + {w} minutes = {hm(r + w)}

distractors.feedback: {clock(value)} leaves time to get ready but not the {w} minutes of walking.
{clock(value)} leaves time to walk but not the {hm(r)} of getting ready.

templates.construct: Change Philippine time to the time in another country

formats.prompt: {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')} is {k} hour{k == 1 ? '' : 's'} {off > 0 ? 'ahead of' : 'behind'} Manila. When it is {clock(t)} in Manila, what time is it in {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')}?

hints: {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')} is {off > 0 ? 'ahead of' : 'behind'} Manila, so {off > 0 ? 'add' : 'take away'} the hours.
{off > 0 ? 'Add' : 'Take away'} {k} hour{k == 1 ? '' : 's'}.
templates.explain: When it is {clock(t)} in Manila, it is {clock(answer)} in {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')}.

distractors.feedback: {clock(value)} goes the wrong way. {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')} is {off > 0 ? 'ahead of' : 'behind'} Manila, so its clocks show {off > 0 ? 'a later' : 'an earlier'} time.

templates.construct: Change the time in another country to Philippine time

formats.prompt: Tita Liza works in {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')}, which is {k} hour{k == 1 ? '' : 's'} {off > 0 ? 'ahead of' : 'behind'} Manila. She calls home at {clock(t)}, {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')} time. What time is it in Manila?

hints: Manila is {off > 0 ? 'behind' : 'ahead of'} {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')}.
So {off > 0 ? 'take away' : 'add'} {k} hour{k == 1 ? '' : 's'}.
templates.explain: When it is {clock(t)} in {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')}, it is {clock(answer)} in Manila.

distractors.feedback: {clock(value)} goes the wrong way. Manila is {k} hour{k == 1 ? '' : 's'} {off > 0 ? 'behind' : 'ahead of'} {pick(p, 'Tokyo', 'Seoul', 'Bangkok', 'Jakarta', 'Dubai', 'Riyadh')}, so {off > 0 ? 'take the hours away' : 'add the hours'}.
